result.title: The Matthews Correlation Coefficient: Fifty years
result.summary: Fifty years after its introduction, the Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) remains central -and debated- in binary classification. This survey offers a comprehensive retrospective and an in-depth analysis of MCC, covering its historical development, mathematical foundations, and implications for practice. We clarify long-standing misconceptions, formalize its equivalences (to Pearson's correlation and to Chi2 in 2x2 tables), and examine its behavior under class imbalance. Beyond MCC, we develop analytical (derivatives) and graphical (contour plots) frameworks that generalize to any confusion-matrix-based metric. These frameworks expose structural properties -bias, robustness, sensitivity- that scalar summaries conceal, and they provide actionable guidance for selecting and interpreting performance measures in applications where reliability and fairness matter. Together, our results position MCC within a broader toolkit while clarifying when it is informative -and when alternatives may be preferable.

AI.brief_summary: 该文综述 Matthews 相关系数（MCC）五十年来的历史、数学基础与实践含义，澄清常见误解，形式化其与 Pearson 相关及 2×2 表 Chi2 的等价性，并用导数与等高线框架分析其在类别不平衡下的偏差、鲁棒性与敏感性。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 latent visual reasoning 无直接联系，但其对不平衡条件下二分类指标偏差与敏感性的分析，可能可供核查用于评价「继续思考/继续看/停止」等二元决策及证据筛选效果的指标选择。
